cues.en: I first saw this pattern that I'm about to show you in a question on the Math Stack Exchange.
cues.zh: 我第一次看到接下来要展示的这个模式，是在 Math Stack Exchange 的一个问题里。

cues.en: It was asked by a user under the name Dwy Mark and answered by Greg Martin, and it relates to the distribution of prime numbers together with rational approximations for pi.
cues.zh: 这个问题由用户 Dwy Mark 提出，Greg Martin 回答，内容涉及质数分布以及 π 的有理逼近。

cues.en: You see what the user had been doing was playing around with data in polar coordinates.
cues.zh: 其实这位用户是在摆弄极坐标里的数据。

cues.en: As a quick reminder, so we're all on the same page, this means labeling points in two d space not with the usual x y coordinates,
cues.zh: 快速提醒一下，统一一下说法：这就是给二维空间中的点标位置时，不用通常的 x、y 坐标，

cues.en: but instead with a distance from the origin,
cues.zh: 而是用离原点的距离，

cues.en: commonly called r for radius,
cues.zh: 通常记作 r，代表半径，

cues.en: together with the angle that that radial line makes with the horizontal,
cues.zh: 再加上这条径向线与水平方向形成的夹角，

cues.en: commonly called theta.
cues.zh: 通常记作 θ。

cues.en: And for our purposes, this angle will be measured in radians,
cues.zh: 在我们这里，这个角度用弧度来度量，

cues.en: which basically means that an angle of pi is halfway around,
cues.zh: 这基本上意味着角度 π 就是半圈，

cues.en: and then two pi is a full circle.
cues.zh: 而 2π 就是一整圈。

cues.en: And notice polar coordinates are not unique in the sense that adding two pi to that second coordinate doesn't change the location that this pair of numbers is referring to.
cues.zh: 注意，极坐标并不唯一：给第二个坐标加上 2π，并不会改变这对数所指的位置。

cues.en: The pattern that we'll look at centers around plotting points where both of these coordinates are a given prime number.
cues.zh: 我们要看的这个模式，核心是画出两个坐标都等于某个给定质数的点。

cues.en: There is no practical reason to do this. It's purely fun. We're just frolicking around in the playground of data visualization.
cues.zh: 这么做没有什么实际理由。纯粹是为了好玩。我们就是在数据可视化的游乐场里闲逛。

cues.en: And to get a sense for what it means, look at all the whole numbers rather than just the primes.
cues.zh: 要想感受它意味着什么，可以看看所有整数，而不只是质数。

cues.en: The point one one sits a distance one away from the origin with an angle of one radian,
cues.zh: 点 (1, 1) 距离原点为 1，对应的夹角是 1 弧度，

cues.en: which actually means this arc is the same length as that radial line.
cues.zh: 这实际上意味着这段弧长和那条半径是相等的。

cues.en: And then two two has twice that angle and twice the distance.
cues.zh: 然后点 (2, 2) 的角度和距离都是它的两倍。

cues.en: And to get to three three, you rotate one more radian a total angle that's now slightly less than a half turn since three is slightly less than pi, and you step one unit farther away from the origin.
cues.zh: 要到达点 (3, 3)，你需要再旋转 1 弧度，此时的总角度略小于半圈，因为 3 略小于 $\pi$，并且你要从原点再向外走一个单位。

cues.en: I really want you to make sure that it's clear what's being plotted because everything that follows depends on understanding it. Each step forward is like the tip of a clock hand, rotates one radian with each tick a little less than a sixth of a turn, and it grows by one unit at each step.
cues.zh: 我真的希望大家能弄清楚这里绘制的到底是什么，因为后面的一切都建立在这个理解之上。每向前一步就像时钟指针的尖端，每一次走动旋转 1 弧度（略小于一整圈的六分之一），并且每一步都增长一个单位。

cues.en: As you continue, these points spiral outwards forming what's known in the business as an Archimedean spiral.
cues.zh: 随着你继续下去，这些点向外盘旋，形成了业内所谓的阿基米德螺线。

cues.en: Now if you make the admittedly arbitrary move to knock out everything except the prime numbers,
cues.zh: 现在，如果你做一个公认是随意的举动，剔除掉除了素数之外的一切，

cues.en: it initially looks quite random. After all, primes are famous for their chaotic and difficult to predict behavior.
cues.zh: 起初它看起来相当随机。毕竟，素数以其混乱且难以预测的行为而闻名。

cues.en: But when you zoom out,
cues.zh: 但当你缩小视野时，

cues.en: what you start to see are these very clear galactic seeming spirals.
cues.zh: 你开始看到的是这些非常清晰的、类似星系般的螺旋。

cues.en: And what's weird is some of the arms seem to be missing.
cues.zh: 诡异的是，其中一些旋臂似乎消失了。

cues.en: Then zooming out even further,
cues.zh: 接着进一步缩小视野，

cues.en: those spirals give way to a different pattern.
cues.zh: 这些螺旋让位于一种不同的图案。

cues.en: These many different outward pointing rays.
cues.zh: 这些许许多多向外指出的射线。

cues.en: And those rays seem to mostly come in clumps of four,
cues.zh: 而且这些射线似乎大多以四条为一组聚集在一起，

cues.en: but there's the occasional gap, like a comb missing its teeth.
cues.zh: 但偶尔会出现空隙，就像一把缺了齿的梳子。

cues.en: The question for you and me naturally is what on earth is going on here? Where do these spirals come from, and why do we instead get straight lines at this larger scale?
cues.zh: 你我自然要问，这到底是怎么回事？这些螺旋从何而来，为什么在更大的尺度上我们反而得到直线？

cues.en: If you wanted, you could ask a more quantitative question and count that there are 20 total spirals.
cues.zh: 如果你愿意，可以问一个更定量的问题，数一数一共有20条螺旋。

cues.en: And then up at that larger scale, if you patiently went through each ray, you'd count up a total of 280.
cues.zh: 然后在更大的尺度上，如果你耐心地走过每条射线，你会数出总共280条。

cues.en: And so this adds a further mystery of where these numbers are coming from and why they would arise from primes.
cues.zh: 这就增添了又一个谜团：这些数字从何而来，为什么它们会从质数中出现？

cues.en: Now this is shocking and beautiful, and you might think that it suggests some divine hidden symmetry within the primes.
cues.zh: 这既令人震惊又优美，你可能会觉得它暗示了质数中某种神圣的隐藏对称性。

cues.en: But to steady your expectations,
cues.zh: 但为了让你的期望更平稳，

cues.en: I should say that the fact that the person asking this question on Math Exchange jumped right into prime numbers makes the puzzle a little misleading.
cues.zh: 我应该说，在Math Exchange上提出这个问题的人直接跳进了质数，这让这个谜题有点误导性。

cues.en: If you look at all of the whole numbers, not just the primes,
cues.zh: 如果你看所有的整数，而不只是质数，

cues.en: As you zoom out, you see very similar spirals.
cues.zh: 当你缩小时，你会看到非常相似的螺旋。

cues.en: They're much cleaner,
cues.zh: 它们干净得多，

cues.en: and now there's 44 of them instead of 20, but it means that the question of where the spirals come from is perhaps disappointingly
cues.zh: 现在有44条而不是20条，但这意味着螺旋从何而来的问题或许令人失望地

cues.en: completely separate from the question of what happens when we limit our view to primes.
cues.zh: 完全独立于当我们把视野限制在质数时会发生什么的问题。

cues.en: But don't be too disappointed because both these questions are still phenomenal puzzles.
cues.zh: 但不要太失望，因为这两个问题仍然是非凡的谜题。

cues.en: There's a very satisfying answer for the spirals.
cues.zh: 对于螺旋有一个非常令人满意的答案。

cues.en: And even if the primes don't cause the spirals, asking what goes on when you filter for those primes does lead you to one of the most important theorems about the distribution of prime numbers, known in number theory as Dirichlet's theorem.
cues.zh: 即使质数不是螺旋的原因，追问当你筛选那些质数时会发生什么，确实会引导你走向关于质数分布的最重要定理之一，在数论中被称为Dirichlet定理。

cues.en: To kick things off, let's zoom back in a little bit smaller.
cues.zh: 为了抛砖引玉，让我们把视角稍微放大一点。

cues.en: Did you notice that as we were zooming out, there were these six little spirals?
cues.zh: 你有没有注意到，当我们缩小视角时，有这六个小螺旋？

cues.en: This offers a good starting point to explain what's happening in the two larger patterns. Notice how all the multiples of six form one arm of this spiral.
cues.zh: 这为解释这两个较大图案中发生的事情提供了一个良好的起点。注意所有六的倍数是如何构成这个螺旋的一条臂的。

cues.en: Then the next one is every integer that's one above a multiple of six.
cues.zh: 然后下一个是所有比六的倍数大一的整数。

cues.en: Then after that, it includes all the numbers two above a multiple of six and so on. Why is that?
cues.zh: 接着是所有比六的倍数大二的数字，以此类推。这是为什么呢？

cues.en: Well, remember that each step forward in the sequence involves a turn of one radian. So when you count up by six, you've turned a total of six radians, which is a little bit less than two pi, a full turn. So every time you count up by six, you've almost made a full turn. It's just a little less.
cues.zh: 嗯，记住序列中的每向前一步都涉及转动一弧度。所以当你以六为单位向上数时，你总共转了六弧度，这比整整一圈的二派（2π）稍微少一点。因此，每次你数六个数，你几乎转完了一整圈。只是稍微少了一点点。

cues.en: Another six steps, a slightly smaller angle.
cues.zh: 再走六步，角度稍微小一点。

cues.en: Six more steps, smaller still, and so on, with this angle changing gently enough that it gives the illusion of a single curving line.
cues.zh: 再走六步，角度更小，以此类推，这个角度变化得足够平缓，从而给人一种单条曲线的错觉。

cues.en: When you limit the view to prime numbers,
cues.zh: 当你把视野限制在质数时，

cues.en: all but two of these spiral arms, they'll go away.
cues.zh: 除了其中的两个螺旋臂之外，其余的都会消失。

cues.en: And think about it. A prime number can't be a multiple of six,
cues.zh: 仔细想想。质数不可能是六的倍数，

cues.en: and it also can't be two above a multiple of six unless it's two or four above a multiple of six since all of those are even numbers.
cues.zh: 而且它也不可能是比六的倍数大二的数，除非它本身就是二，或者比六的倍数大四，因为所有这些都是偶数。

cues.en: It also can't be three above a multiple of six unless it's the number three itself since all of those are divisible by three.
cues.zh: 它也不可能是比六的倍数大三的数，除非它本身就是数字三，因为所有这些都能被三整除。

cues.en: So at least at this smaller scale, nothing magical is going on. And while we're in the simpler context, let me introduce some terminology that mathematicians use. Each one of these sequences where you're counting up by six is fancifully called a residue class mod six.
cues.zh: 所以至少在这个较小的尺度上，并没有什么神奇的事情。趁着现在情况还简单，我来介绍几个数学家常用的术语。每一个每次递增 6 的序列，在数学上被花哨地称为“模 6 的剩余类”。

cues.en: The word residue here is sort of an overdramatic way of saying remainder,
cues.zh: 这里的“剩余”其实就是对“余数”一种有点夸张的叫法，

cues.en: and mod means something like where the thing you divide by is.
cues.zh: 而“模”大概指的就是你除以的那个数。

cues.en: So for example, six goes into 23
cues.zh: 比如，20 可以被 6 除 3

cues.en: times, and it leaves a remainder of two.
cues.zh: 次，并且余数是 2。

cues.en: So 20 has a residue of two mod six.
cues.zh: 所以 20 模 6 的剩余就是 2。

cues.en: Together with all the other numbers leaving a remainder of two when the thing you divide by is six,
cues.zh: 把所有除以 6 同样余 2 的数字放在一起，

cues.en: you have a full residue class mod six.
cues.zh: 就构成了一个完整的模 6 剩余类。

cues.en: I know that that sounds like the world's most pretentious way of saying everything too above a multiple of six,
cues.zh: 我知道这听起来像是全世界最装腔作势的说法，其实意思就是“比 6 的倍数大 2 的所有数”，

cues.en: but this is the standard jargon, and it is actually handy to have some words for the idea.
cues.zh: 但这是标准的专业术语，而且用专门的词来表达这个概念确实挺方便的。

cues.en: So looking at our diagram, in the lingo, each of these spiral arms corresponds to a residue class mod six, and the reason we see them is that six is close to two pi. Turning six radians is almost a full turn.
cues.zh: 回到图表上，用行话来说，每条螺旋臂都对应一个模 6 的剩余类；我们能看到它们，是因为 6 很接近 2π，转动 6 弧度差不多就是转了一整圈。

cues.en: And the reason we see only two of them when filtering for primes is that all prime numbers are either one or five above a multiple of six with the exceptions of two and three.
cues.zh: 而筛选质数时之所以只剩下两条，是因为除了 2 和 3，所有质数要么比 6 的倍数大 1，要么大 5。

cues.en: With all that as a warm up, let's think about the larger scale. In the same way that six steps is close to a full turn,
cues.zh: 有了这些做铺垫，我们来看看更大的尺度。就像走 6 步接近转了一整圈一样，

cues.en: taking 44 steps is very close to a whole number of turns. Here, let's compute it.
cues.zh: 走 44 步也非常接近转了整数圈。来，我们算一下。

cues.en: There are two pi radians per rotation. Right? So taking 44 steps, turning 44 radians, gives a total of 44 divided by two pi rotations,
cues.zh: 一整圈是 2π 弧度，对吧？所以走 44 步、转过 44 弧度，相当于转了 44 除以 2π 圈，

cues.en: which comes out to be just barely above seven full turns.
cues.zh: 结果刚刚超过七整圈。

cues.en: You could also write this by saying that 44 sevenths is a close approximation for two pi, which some of you may better recognize as the famous 22 sevenths approximation for pi.
cues.zh: 也可以说，44/7 近似等于 2π；你们有些人可能更熟悉它的另一种写法：著名的 π≈22/7。

cues.en: What this means is when you count up by multiples of 44 in the diagram,
cues.zh: 这意味着，在图中每次按 44 的倍数递增时，

cues.en: each point has almost the same angle as the last one, just a little bit bigger. So as you continue on with more and more, we get this very gentle spiral as the angle increases very slowly.
cues.zh: 每个点的角度都几乎和上一个相同，只是略大一点。随着数字不断增大，角度缓慢增加，就会形成这条非常平缓的螺旋线。

cues.en: Similarly, all the numbers one above a multiple of 44 make another spiral, but rotated one radian counterclockwise.
cues.zh: 同样，所有比 44 的倍数大 1 的数会形成另一条螺旋线，它逆时针旋转 1 弧度。

cues.en: Same for everything two above a multiple of 44 and so on, eventually filling out the full diagram.
cues.zh: 比 44 的倍数大 2 的数也一样，依此类推，最终铺满整张图。

cues.en: To phrase it with our fancier language, each of these spiral arms shows a residue class mod 44.
cues.zh: 用更专业的说法，每条螺旋臂都表示一个模 44 的剩余类。

cues.en: And maybe now you can tell me what happens when we limit our view to prime numbers.
cues.zh: 现在你们大概能说出，只看质数时会发生什么了。

cues.en: Primes cannot be a multiple of 44, so that arm won't be visible.
cues.zh: 质数不可能是 44 的倍数，所以那条螺旋臂不会出现。

cues.en: Nor can a prime be two above a multiple of 44 or four above and so on, since all those residue classes have nothing but even numbers.
cues.zh: 质数也不可能比 44 的倍数大 2、大 4，依此类推，因为这些剩余类里全是偶数。

cues.en: Likewise, any multiples of 11 can't be prime except for 11 itself.
cues.zh: 同样，11 的倍数也不可能是质数，除了 11 本身。

cues.en: So the spiral of numbers 11 above a multiple of 44, they won't be visible, and neither will the spiral of numbers 33 above a multiple of 44.
cues.zh: 所以，比 44 的倍数大 11 的那些数形成的螺旋线不会出现，比 44 的倍数大 33 的那些数形成的螺旋线也不会出现。

cues.en: This is what gives the picture those Milky Way seeming gaps.
cues.zh: 这赋予了图中那些看似银河系的空隙。

cues.en: Each spiral we're left with is a residue class that doesn't share any prime factors with 44.
cues.zh: 我们剩下的每条螺旋都是一个与 44 不共享任何质因数的剩余类。

cues.en: And within each one of those arms that we can't reject out of hand, the prime numbers seem to be sort of randomly distributed.
cues.zh: 而在那些不能直接排除的旋臂中，素数似乎有些随机分布。

cues.en: And that's a fact that I'd like you to tuck away. We'll return to it later.
cues.zh: 这个事实请你们先记住，我们稍后会回到它。

cues.en: This is another good chance to inject some of the jargon that mathematicians use. What we care about right here are all the numbers between zero and forty three that don't share a prime factor with 44. Right? The ones that aren't even, and they also aren't divisible by 11.
cues.zh: 这是引入数学家行话的又一个好机会。这里我们关心的是 0 到 43 之间所有与 44 不共享质因数的数，对吧？也就是那些不是偶数，同时也不能被 11 整除的数。

cues.en: When two numbers don't share any factors like this,
cues.zh: 当两个数像这样不共享任何因数时，

cues.en: we call them relatively prime or also co prime.
cues.zh: 我们称它们互质，也叫互素。

cues.en: In this example, you could count that there are 20 different numbers between one and forty four that are co prime to 44.
cues.zh: 在这个例子中，你可以数出 1 到 44 之间有 20 个不同的数与 44 互质。

cues.en: And this is a fact that a number theorist would compactly write by saying phi of 44 equals 20, where the Greek letter phi here refers to Euler's totient function, yet another needlessly fancy word, which is defined to be the number of integers from one up to n, which are co prime to n.
cues.zh: 数论学家会简洁地写成 φ(44) = 20，这里的希腊字母 φ 指欧拉函数，又一个没必要花哨的词，它的定义是 1 到 n 中与 n 互质的整数个数。

cues.en: It comes up enough that it's handy to have compact notation.
cues.zh: 它出现得够频繁，所以有个简洁记号会很方便。

cues.en: More obscurely, and I had never heard this before, but I find it too delightful not to tell, these numbers are sometimes called the totatives of n.
cues.zh: 更冷门的是——我以前从没听过，但觉得太有趣了，不能不提——这些数有时被称为 n 的 totatives。

cues.en: Back to the main thread, in short, what the user on Math Exchange was seeing are two unrelated pieces of number theory, but illustrated in one drawing.
cues.zh: 回到主线，简单来说，Math Exchange 上的那位用户所看到的，其实是两个互不相关的数论现象，只是呈现在了同一张图里。

cues.en: The first is that 44 sevenths is a very close rational approximation for two pi, which results in the residue classes mod 44
cues.zh: 第一点是，44/7 是 2π 的一个非常接近的有理逼近，这使得模 44 的剩余类

cues.en: being cleanly separated out.
cues.zh: 能够被清晰地分离开来。

cues.en: The second is that many of these residue classes contain zero prime numbers or sometimes just one, so they won't show up. But on the other hand, primes do show up plentifully enough in all 20 of the other residue classes that it makes these spiral arms visible.
cues.zh: 第二点是，这些剩余类中很多包含零个质数，或者偶尔只有一个，所以它们不会显现出来。但另一方面，质数在其余全部 20 个剩余类中出现得足够频繁，从而让这些螺旋臂清晰可见。

cues.en: And at this point, maybe you can predict what's going on at the larger scale.
cues.zh: 看到这里，你也许就能猜到在更大尺度上会发生什么了。

cues.en: Just as six radians is vaguely close to a full turn and 44 radians is quite close to seven full turns,
cues.zh: 就像 6 弧度大致接近一整圈，而 44 弧度非常接近 7 整圈一样，

cues.en: it just so happens that 710
cues.zh: 碰巧 710

cues.en: radians is extremely close to a whole number of full turns.
cues.zh: 弧度极其接近整数圈整转。

cues.en: Visually, you can see this by the fact that the point ends up almost exactly on the x axis, but it's more compelling analytically.
cues.zh: 直观上，你可以看到这个点几乎刚好落在 x 轴上，但从代数分析上看更有说服力。

cues.en: 710 radians is 710 divided by two pi rotations,
cues.zh: 710 弧度就是 710 除以 2π 圈，

cues.en: which works out to be a 113.0000095.
Some of you may have seen this in another form. It's saying that seven hundred ten one hundred thirteenths is a close approximation for two pi, which is more commonly seen in saying that 355
cues.zh: 你们有些人可能见过它的另一种形式。这相当于说 710/113 是 2π 的极佳逼近，而更常见的表述是 355

cues.en: over a 113
cues.zh: 比上 113

cues.en: is a very good approximation for pi.
cues.zh: 是 π 的极佳逼近。

cues.en: Now if you wanna understand where these rational approximations are coming from and what it means for one like this to be unusually good, like way better than you would get for phi or e or square root of two or other famous irrationals,
cues.zh: 如果你想弄明白这些有理逼近是怎么来的，以及为什么像这样的逼近会好得不可思议——远好于黄金比例 φ、e、根号 2 或其他著名无理数上的逼近——

cues.en: I highly recommend taking a look at this great mythologer video.
cues.zh: 我强烈推荐看一看 mythologer 的这个精彩视频。

cues.en: For our storyline though, it means that when you move forward by steps of 710,
cues.zh: 不过在我们的故事线里，它的意思是：每次向前走 710 步时，

cues.en: the angle of each new point is almost exactly the same as the last one, just microscopically
cues.zh: 每个新点的角度几乎和前一个完全一样，只是微乎其微地改变了一点

cues.en: bigger.
cues.zh: 更大。

cues.en: Even very far out, one of these sequences looks like a straight line.
cues.zh: 即使在很远处，其中一个序列看起来也像一条直线。

cues.en: And, of course, the other residue classes mod 710
cues.zh: 当然，还有模 710 的其他剩余类。

cues.en: also form these nearly straight lines.
cues.zh: 这些也几乎形成直线。

cues.en: 710 is a big number, though. So when all of them are on screen and there's only so many pixels on the screen, it's a little hard to make them out.
cues.zh: 不过710是个大数字。当它们全都显示在屏幕上，而屏幕像素又有限时，就有点难辨认了。

cues.en: So in this case, it's actually easier to see when we limit the view to primes where you don't see many of those residue classes.
cues.zh: 所以在这个情况下，当我们把视野限制在那些看不到很多剩余类的素数时，其实更容易看出来。

cues.en: In reality, with a little further zooming, you can see that there actually is a very gentle spiral to these. But the fact that it takes so long to become prominent is a wonderful illustration,
cues.zh: 实际上，再稍微放大一点，你就能看到它们其实呈一条非常平缓的螺旋。但要过很久才变得显著，这一点绝佳地说明了，

cues.en: maybe the best illustration I've ever seen for just how good an approximation this is for two pi.
cues.zh: 也许这是我见过的、最能说明它对2π的近似有多好的例子。

cues.en: Tying up the remaining loose thread here, if you wanna understand what happens when you filter for primes, it's entirely analogous to what we did before. The factors of 710
cues.zh: 收尾处理剩下的这根琐碎线程，如果你想理解当你筛选素数时发生了什么，它和我们之前做的事情完全类似。710的因数

cues.en: are 71,
five, and two.
cues.zh: 五，还有二。

cues.en: So if the remainder or residue is divisible by any of those, then so is the number.
cues.zh: 所以如果余数能被其中任何一个整除，那么这个数也能被整除。

cues.en: When you pull up all of the residue classes with odd numbers,
cues.zh: 当你把所有由奇数构成的剩余类列出来时，

cues.en: it looks like every other ray in the otherwise quite crowded picture.
cues.zh: 它看起来就像那张原本相当拥挤的图片中的其他任何光线一样。

cues.en: And then of those that remain, these are the ones that are divisible by five, which are nice and evenly spaced at every fifth line.
cues.zh: 然后在剩下的里面，这些是能被 5 整除的，它们整整齐齐地每隔五行出现一次。

cues.en: Notice the fact that prime numbers never show up in any of these is what explains the pattern of the lines we saw at the beginning coming in clumps of four.
cues.zh: 注意到了吗，质数绝不会出现在其中，这正是为什么我们开头看到的线条是四条一组扎堆出现的。

cues.en: And moreover,
cues.zh: 不仅如此，

cues.en: of those remaining,
cues.zh: 在剩下的这些当中，

cues.en: these four residue classes are the ones that are divisible by 71. So the primes aren't gonna show up there, and that's what explains why the clumps of four that we saw occasionally have, like, a missing tooth in your comb.
cues.zh: 这四个剩余类能被 71 整除。所以质数也不会出现在这里，这就解释了为什么那些四条一组的线条偶尔会像梳子缺了齿一样。

cues.en: And if you were wondering where that number 280 came from, it comes from counting how many of the numbers from one up to 710
cues.zh: 如果你好奇 280 这个数字是怎么来的，它其实是统计了从 1 到 710 的数字中，有多少个

cues.en: don't share any prime factors with 710.
cues.zh: 和 710 没有共同的质因数。

cues.en: These are the ones that we can't rule out for including primes based on some obvious divisibility consideration.
cues.zh: 仅凭显而易见的整除规则，我们无法排除它们包含质数的可能。

cues.en: This, of course, doesn't guarantee that any particular one will contain prime numbers, but at least empirically, when you look at this picture, it actually seems like the primes are pretty evenly distributed among the remaining classes. Wouldn't you agree?
cues.zh: 当然，这并不保证特定的某个类里就一定有质数，但至少从直观上看，从这张图里看，质数在剩下的类中分布得相当均匀，不是吗？

cues.en: This last point is actually the most interesting observation of the whole deal. It relates to a pretty deep fact in number theory known as Dirichlet's theorem. To take a simpler example than residue classes mod seven ten, think of those mod 10.
cues.zh: 最后这一点其实是整个过程中最有趣的发现。它涉及数论中一个相当深刻的结论，即狄利克雷定理（Dirichlet's theorem）。举个比模 710 剩余类更简单的例子，我们可以看看模 10 的情况。

cues.en: Because we write numbers in base 10, this is the same thing as grouping numbers together by what their last digit is.
cues.zh: 因为我们用十进制写数，所以这等同于按个位数字把数分组。

cues.en: Everything whose last digit is zero is a residue class, everything whose last digit is one is another residue class, and so on.
cues.zh: 所有个位为 0 的数构成一个剩余类，所有个位为 1 的数构成另一个剩余类，以此类推。

cues.en: Other than two, prime numbers can't have an even number as their last digit since that means they're even.
cues.zh: 除了 2 以外，质数的个位不可能是偶数，因为那意味着它们本身是偶数。

cues.en: And likewise, any prime bigger than five can't end in a five. There's nothing surprising there. That's one of the first facts you observe when you learn about prime numbers. Anything bigger than five has to end in either a one, a three, a seven, or a nine.
cues.zh: 同样，任何大于 5 的质数都不能以 5 结尾。这没什么好奇怪的。这是你学习质数时最早观察到的事实之一。任何大于 5 的质数，个位都只能是 1、3、7 或 9。

cues.en: A much more nuanced question though is how exactly these primes are divvied up among those remaining four groups.
cues.zh: 不过，一个微妙得多的问题是：这些质数究竟是如何分配到最后这四个组里的。

cues.en: Here, let's make a quick histogram counting through each prime number where the bars are gonna show what proportion of the primes that we've seen so far have a given last digit.
cues.zh: 这里，我们快速做一个直方图，逐个统计每个质数，柱子将显示到目前为止我们见过的质数中，有多大比例具有某个给定的个位数字。

cues.en: So in particular, the two and the five slots should go down to zero over time.
cues.zh: 所以特别是，2 和 5 这两个槽位会随着时间降到零。

cues.en: What would you predict is gonna happen as we move through more and more primes?
cues.zh: 随着我们考察越来越多质数，你预测会发生什么？

cues.en: Well,
cues.zh: 嗯，

cues.en: as we get a lot of them, it seems like a pretty even spread between these four classes,
cues.zh: 当我们得到很多质数时，看起来它们在这四个类之间的分布相当均匀，

cues.en: about 25%
cues.zh: 大约 25%

cues.en: each. And probably that's what you would expect. After all, why would prime numbers show some sort of preference for one last digit over another?
cues.zh: 每个。而且这很可能正是你所预料的。毕竟，质数为什么会偏爱某个个位数字而不是另一个呢？

cues.en: But primes aren't random. They are a definite sequence, and they show patterns in other ways, and it's highly non obvious how you would prove something like this.
cues.zh: 但质数并不是随机的。它们是一个确定的序列，也会以其他方式表现出规律，而如何证明这样的事情是非常不显然的。

cues.en: Or for that matter, how do you rigorously phrase what it is that you want to prove?
cues.zh: 或者说，你如何严谨地表述你想证明的东西？

cues.en: A mathematician might go about it something like this.
cues.zh: 数学家可能会这样做。

cues.en: If you look at all the prime numbers less than some big number x
cues.zh: 如果你考虑所有小于某个大数 x 的质数

cues.en: and you consider what fraction of them are, say, one above a multiple of 10,
cues.zh: 然后考虑其中有几分之几，比如说，是比 10 的倍数大 1，

cues.en: that fraction should approach one fourth as x approaches infinity.
cues.zh: 当 x 趋近于无穷大时，这个比例应该趋近于四分之一。

cues.en: And likewise for all of the other allowable residue classes, like three and seven and nine.
cues.zh: 对于其他所有允许的剩余类，比如 3、7 和 9，也同样如此。

cues.en: Of course, there's nothing special about 10. A similar fact should hold for any other number. Considering our old friends, the residue classes mod 44, for example, let's make a similar histogram showing what proportion of the primes show up in each one of these.
cues.zh: 当然，10 并没有什么特别之处。类似的事实对任何其他数也应该成立。想想我们的老朋友，比如模 44 的剩余类，让我们做一个类似的直方图，显示每个剩余类中出现质数的比例。

cues.en: Again,
cues.zh: 再次，

cues.en: as time goes on, we see an even spread between the 20 different allowable residue classes, which you can think of in terms of each spiral arm from our diagram having about the same number of primes as each of the others.
cues.zh: 随着时间的推移，我们看到 20 个不同的允许剩余类之间呈现均匀分布，你可以理解为图中每条螺旋臂上的质数数量大致相同。

cues.en: Maybe that's what you'd expect, but this is a shockingly hard fact to prove.
cues.zh: 也许这正是你所预料的，但这是一个极其难以证明的事实。

cues.en: The first man who cracked this puzzle was Dirichlet in 1837,
cues.zh: 第一个破解这个谜题的人是 1837 年的 Dirichlet，

cues.en: and it forms one of the crowning jewels at the foundation of modern analytic number theory.
cues.zh: 它构成了现代解析数论基础的皇冠上的明珠之一。

cues.en: Histograms like these ones give a pretty good illustration of what the theorem is actually saying. Nevertheless, you might find it enlightening to see how it might be written in a math text with all the fancy jargon and everything. It's essentially what we just saw for 10, but more general.
cues.zh: 像这样的直方图很好地说明了这个定理实际上在说什么。不过，你可能会发现，看看它在数学教科书中如何用各种花哨的术语来表述，也许会很有启发性。它本质上就是我们刚才看到的关于 10 的情况，但更一般化。

cues.en: Again, you look at all of the primes up to some bound x, but instead of asking for what proportion of them have a residue of, say, one mod 10,
cues.zh: 同样地，你考察所有不超过某个上限x的素数，但不是问它们中有多大比例除以10余1，

cues.en: you ask what proportion have a residue of r mod n,
cues.zh: 而是问有多大比例除以n余r，

cues.en: where n is any number and r is anything that's co prime to n. Remember, that means it doesn't share any factors with n bigger than one.
cues.zh: 其中n是任意数，r是任何与n互质的数。记住，这意味着它和n不共享任何大于1的因子。

cues.en: Instead of approaching one fourth as x goes to infinity, that proportion goes to one divided by phi of n,
cues.zh: 当x趋于无穷时，这个比例不是趋近于四分之一，而是趋近于1除以phi(n)，

cues.en: where phi is that special function I mentioned earlier that gives the number of possible residues co prime to n.
cues.zh: 其中phi是我之前提到的那个特殊函数，它给出与n互质的可能余数的个数。

cues.en: And in case this is too clear for the reader, you might see it buried in more notation where this denominator and the numerator are both written with a special prime counting function.
cues.zh: 如果这对读者来说还不够清楚，你可能会看到它被埋在更多符号里，其中分母和分子都用特殊的素数计数函数来写。

cues.en: The convention rather confusingly is to use the symbol pi for this function even though it's totally unrelated to the number pi.
cues.zh: 相当令人困惑的惯例是用符号pi来表示这个函数，尽管它与数字pi完全无关。

cues.en: In some contexts, when people refer to Dirichlet's theorem, they refer to a much more modest statement, which is simply that each of these residue classes that might have infinitely many primes does have infinitely many.
cues.zh: 在某些语境下，人们提到Dirichlet定理时，指的是一个温和得多的陈述，即这些可能含有无穷多个素数的剩余类中，每一个确实都含有无穷多个素数。

cues.en: In order to prove this, what Dirichlet did was show that the primes are just as dense in any one of these residue classes as in any other.
cues.zh: 为了证明这一点，Dirichlet所做的就是证明素数在任何一个这样的剩余类中的密度都与其他剩余类相同。

cues.en: For example, imagine someone asked you to prove that there are infinitely many primes ending in the number one, and the way you do it is by showing that a quarter of all the primes end in a one. Together with the fact that there are infinitely many primes, which we've known since Euclid,
cues.zh: 例如，想象有人让你证明有无穷多个以数字1结尾的素数，你的做法是证明所有素数中有四分之一以1结尾。再加上自Euclid以来我们就知道的素数有无穷多个这一事实，

cues.en: this gives a stronger statement and a much more interesting one.
cues.zh: 这就给出了一个更强的陈述，也是一个有趣得多的陈述。

cues.en: Now the proof,
cues.zh: 现在来证明这个结论，

cues.en: well, it's way more involved than would be reasonable to show here. One interesting fact worth mentioning is that it relies heavily on complex analysis,
cues.zh: 嗯，这个证明比在这里展示合理范围内的内容要复杂得多。值得一提的是，它高度依赖复分析，

cues.en: which is the study of doing calculus with functions whose inputs and outputs are complex numbers.
cues.zh: 也就是研究输入和输出都是复数的函数，并对这类函数进行微积分。

cues.en: Now that might seem weird. Right? I mean, prime numbers seem wholly unrelated to the continuous world of calculus, much less when complex numbers end up in the mix. But since the early nineteenth century, this is absolutely par for the course when it comes to understanding how primes are distributed.
cues.zh: 这听起来可能很奇怪，对吧？我的意思是，素数似乎和微积分的连续世界完全无关，更不用说还要引入复数了。但从十九世纪初开始，在理解素数如何分布时，这完全就是常规做法。

cues.en: And this isn't just antiquated technology either. Understanding the distribution of primes in residue classes like this continues to be relevant in modern research too. Some of the recent breakthroughs on small gaps between primes edging towards that ever elusive twin prime conjecture have their basis in understanding how primes split up among these kinds of residue classes.
cues.zh: 而且这也不是什么过时的技术。理解素数在这类剩余类中的分布，在现代研究中仍然很重要。近年来关于素数间小间隔的一些突破，正逐渐逼近那个始终难以捉摸的孪生素数猜想，而这些突破的基础之一，就是理解素数如何分布在这类剩余类中。

cues.en: Okay. Looking back over the puzzle, I wanna emphasize something.
cues.zh: 好了，回顾这个谜题时，我想强调一点。

cues.en: The original bit of data visualization
cues.zh: 最初的数据可视化

cues.en: whimsy that led to these patterns,
cues.zh: 以及促成这些模式的奇思妙想，

cues.en: well, like, it doesn't matter. No one cares. There's nothing special about plotting p comma p in polar coordinates. And most of the initial mystery in these spirals resulted from the artifacts that come from dealing with integer number of radians, which is kind of weird.
cues.zh: 嗯，其实都无关紧要。没人关心。把 p、p 画在极坐标中，并没有什么特别之处。而这些螺旋最初带来的神秘感，很大一部分源于使用整数弧度时产生的伪影，这本身就有点奇怪。

cues.en: But on the other hand, this kind of play is clearly worth it if the end result is a line of questions that leads you to something like Dirichlet's theorem, which is important,
cues.zh: 但另一方面，如果最终结果是一连串问题，把你引向像狄利克雷定理这样重要的东西，那这种玩显然是值得的，

cues.en: especially if it inspires you to learn enough to understand the tactics of the underlying proof.
cues.zh: 尤其是当它能启发你学到足够的知识，去理解背后证明的策略时。

cues.en: No small task, by the way.
cues.zh: 顺便说一句，这可不是小事。

cues.en: And this isn't a coincidence that a fairly random question like this can lead you to an important and deep fact for math. What it means for a piece of math to be important and deep is that it connects to many other topics.
cues.zh: 像这样一个相当随机的问题能把你引向数学中一个重要而深刻的事实，这并非巧合。一个数学内容之所以重要而深刻，意味着它与许多其他主题相连。

cues.en: So even an arbitrary exploration of numbers, as long as it's not too arbitrary, has a good chance of stumbling into something meaningful.
cues.zh: 所以即使是对数字的任意探索，只要不太随意，也很可能撞见有意义的东西。

cues.en: Sure. You'll get a much more concentrated dosage of important facts by going through a textbook or a course, and there will be many fewer uninteresting dead ends. But there is something special about rediscovering these topics on your own.
cues.zh: 当然。通过教科书或课程，你会获得浓缩得多的重要事实，死胡同也会少得多。但自己重新发现这些主题，有一种特别之处。

cues.en: If you effectively reinvent Euler's totient function before you've ever seen it defined, or if you start wondering about rational approximations before learning about continued fractions, or if you seriously explore how primes are divvied up between residue classes before you've even heard the name Dirichlet,
cues.zh: 如果你在还没见过欧拉 totient 函数的定义之前就实际上重新发明了它，或者你在学连分数之前就开始琢磨有理逼近，又或者你甚至在听说狄利克雷这个名字之前就认真探索了素数如何在剩余类之间分配，

cues.en: then when you do learn those topics, you'll see them as familiar friends, not as arbitrary definitions.
cues.zh: 那么当你真正学习这些主题时，你会把它们看作熟悉的朋友，而不是随意的定义。

cues.en: And that will almost certainly mean that you learn it more effectively.
cues.zh: 而这几乎肯定意味着你会更有效地学会它。
